tier_reason: The page's embedded BENCHMARK_DATA (run of 2026-09-01) has VTD-XML and libxml2 rows from one harness, and the code is public (bemayer/xml-benchmark benchmarks/vtd-xml/src/main/java/bench/Bench.java, benchmarks/libxml2/bench.cpp). No CPU model is published (only 'ubuntu-latest / GitHub Actions'), so it is not A. The suite is a 1-star repo with no license, created 2026-04-06, so it is not a well-known independent suite and B does not apply. This is C, the same call batch-08 (RapidXML) and batch-35 (quick-xml) made on this suite.

corrections.claimed_speedup:
bemayer/xml-benchmark DOM Parse, run of 2026-09-01 (the page regenerates monthly). Mean times in ms, VTD-XML vs libxml2; all ratios derived from page data:
- 100KB: 0.542 vs 0.871 (1.6x)
- 1MB: 3.439 vs 10.788 (3.1x)
- 10MB: 21.45 vs 104.783 (4.9x)
- 100MB: 238.903 vs 646.685 (2.7x)
- 1KB: 0.036 vs 0.013 (VTD-XML is 2.8x slower)

These ratios are not like-for-like above 1KB. VTD-XML's rows at 100KB-100MB cover only the wide file. VTD-XML's MAX_DEPTH is 254, so it rejects the deep files (1,706-5,000 levels). Throughput x time on the page equals the wide-file size exactly. libxml2's rows average the wide file with a deep file that libxml2 2.9.14 halts at depth 256. Per-shape times are not published, so a same-file ratio cannot be derived.

VTD-XML's 'DOM Parse' builds a VTD token index, not a node tree. libxml2 builds and frees a full xmlDoc.

XPath //*[@id] runs on the same wide-only files for both libraries, and VTD-XML loses at every size:
- 1KB: 0.086 vs 0.005 ms (17x slower)
- 100KB: 0.907 vs 0.126 ms (7.2x slower)
- 1MB: 36.943 vs 2.509 ms (14.7x slower)
- 10MB: 392.963 vs 42.573 ms (9.2x slower)
- 100MB: 3837.515 vs 565.64 ms (6.8x slower)

The page's aggregate score ranks libxml2 (32.5) above VTD-XML (30.5).
corrections.workload: bemayer/xml-benchmark cross-language shootout (14 libraries, 7 languages). Each library runs in its own Docker container on a GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest runner. Time is the mean of N auto-calibrated iterations (the page says 'median', but the harness divides total time by iterations). Each synthetic bucket (nominal 1KB-100MB) averages a wide/shallow file and a deep/narrow file. The deep files are about 5.6 MiB (100KB label), 47.9 MiB (1MB and 10MB labels) and 100 MiB (100MB label), with 1,706-5,000 nesting levels. VTD-XML's DOM Parse is VTDGen.setDoc(xml.clone()) + parse(false), which is namespace-unaware and builds no tree. It has no rows for deep files above 1KB.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: VTD-XML: com.ximpleware:vtd-xml resolved from the Maven range [2.0,), which gives 2.13.4 (Maven Central metadata lastUpdated 2017-08-10). The harness is built with maven:3-eclipse-temurin-21 and runs on eclipse-temurin:21-jre as a plain `java -jar` with no JVM flags. It does min(5, iterations) warm-up parses, and only 1 measured iteration on files over 50 MB. libxml2: Debian bookworm's prebuilt package (2.9.14). Its harness is built with bookworm g++ via cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release (CMake default -O3 -DNDEBUG), C++17. The harness calls xmlParseMemory + xmlFreeDoc with no options (no XML_PARSE_HUGE).
corrections.hardware: GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest runner, with each library in its own Docker container (CPU model not published)

corrections.caveats:
Evidence problems:
- The only head-to-head against libxml2 is bemayer/xml-benchmark, a small third-party suite (1 star, no license, created 2026-04-06). It runs once a month on a shared CI runner with no CPU model.
- Its DOM Parse buckets are not like-for-like. VTD-XML's MAX_DEPTH = 254 (VTDGen.java throws 'Depth exceeds MAX_DEPTH'), so VTD-XML fails on the 1,706-5,000-level deep files, and its 100KB-100MB rows cover only the wide file. libxml2's rows average the wide file with a deep file that libxml2 2.9.14 halts at depth 256. The displayed 1.6x-4.9x ratios therefore compare different file sets.
- VTD-XML's 'DOM Parse' builds a non-extractive token index, not a node tree.

Where VTD-XML loses:
- It is slower than libxml2 on XPath //*[@id] at every size (6.8x-17x).
- It loses DOM Parse at 1KB.
- pugixml beats it at 1KB, 10MB and 100MB.
- The page's aggregate score ranks libxml2 above VTD-XML.

Project limits:
- VTD-XML cannot parse documents deeper than 254 levels in standard mode.
- There has been no release since 2.13.4 (2017). The last GitHub commit is from 2018-06-28.
- The source headers are GPL-2.0-or-later but also cite US patents 7133857, 7260652 and 7761459. They add a clause that terminates the licenses of parties in litigation with XimpleWare, so check before copying.

notes: Numbers on the page match the record exactly. Throughput x time shows that VTD-XML's DOM rows cover only the wide file, because VTD-XML rejects deep files. libxml2's rows include halted deep-file parses, so the per-size ratios are not same-file comparisons, and claimed_speedup was rewritten to say so. Other fixes: the GitHub copy is by SourceForge project member jzhang2004 (the record called it unofficial), the latest release is 2.13.4 (not 2.12), the license is GPL-2.0-or-later per the headers, and maintenance_status is abandoned (last commit 2018-06-28).
